the addition of glucose to fructose or to fructans in solution or food does not prevent symptoms or breath hydrogen responses in patients with fructan or fructose malabsorbtion.
the addition of glucose to fructose in solution or fructose containing whole foods does not prevent symptoms or reduce breath hydrogen in functional bowel disorder patients.
the addition of glucose to fructose or to fructans in solution or in foods does not improve symptoms of fructose malabsorbers.

adding glucose to food or solutions to enhance fructan or fructose absorption is ineffective in preventing fructose malabsorbed induced functional gastrointestinal symptoms.
adding glucose to fructose or FODMAPs does not enhance the absorption of fructans and does not prevent the onset of symptoms.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of glucose to foods or solutions containing fructose in patients with functional gastrointestinal symptoms and/or fructose malabsoprtion is not an effective treatment strategy.
the addition of glucose to fructose in solution or foods does not improve the symptoms of fructose malabsorbers.
the addition of glucose to foods high in fructose or FODMAPs is not recommended to prevent fructose malabsorbtion and associated functional symptoms.

fructose malabsorbers should be encouraged to eat whole fruits and vegetables and to consume them with meals to minimize symptoms.
fructose malabsorbers should be advised to limit their intake of fructose and fructans in foods, and not rely on glucose addition to enhance absorption.
